styleWhy: The video is about words, so the words themselves are the picture: each one lands huge, splits into its Chinese roots, and the wrong guess about it gets struck through.

copy.idea: Four everyday English words (ketchup, tycoon, typhoon, kowtow) have roots in Chinese. Each one hides a surprising original meaning.
copy.hook: You speak a little Chinese already. Four everyday English words started there.
copy.body:
Ketchup: it started as a fermented fish sauce, likely from the Hokkien 'kê-tsiap'. Tomatoes came much later.

Tycoon: the Chinese 'dà jūn', 'great lord', reached English through the Japanese 'taikun', a title used for the shogun.

Typhoon: partly the Chinese 'big wind' (Cantonese 'daai fung'), blended with the Greek storm monster Typhon and the Arabic 'tufan'.

Kowtow: from 'kòu tóu', literally 'knock head', meaning to bow until your forehead touches the ground.

Four words, one language behind them. Which one surprised you?

facts.text: Ketchup likely comes from a Hokkien (Amoy) Chinese word for a brine or sauce of pickled fish, possibly by way of Malay 'kecap'.
Tycoon comes from Japanese 'taikun', a title for the shogun used with foreigners, from Chinese 'great' + 'prince/lord' (大君).
Typhoon is partly from Chinese 'great wind' (Cantonese 'tai fung'), merged with Arabic 'tufan' and Greek 'Typhon'.
Kowtow comes from Chinese 'k'o-t'ou' (叩頭), from 'knock' + 'head', the act of touching the forehead to the ground in respect.

shots.title: Hook: four words
shots.show: Four-word stack: KETCHUP, TYCOON, TYPHOON, KOWTOW slam in one by one, huge, white, filling the frame top to bottom. A big '4' in fire orange rolls up from 1 to 4 beside the stack as each word lands, then an orange marker sweeps across the whole stack.
shots.motion: Each word drops in from above with a short squash bounce (one every 0.5 s), the counter ticks with them, the marker sweep finishes at 3 s and the stack shakes lightly.

shots.title: Ketchup
shots.show: Word card: KETCHUP lands huge at the top in white. Below it the Chinese root 'kê-tsiap' (Hokkien) rises in amber. Then the line 'Started as tomato sauce' types in word by word; 'tomato' is struck through in red and rolls into 'fermented fish', which gets an orange marker sweep. A simple fish icon swims across the empty lower third and a tomato icon fades in last, small, labelled 'later'.
shots.text: Ketchup began as a fermented fish sauce
shots.motion: Word pops, root rises from below, line types, strike-through draws left to right, the struck word rolls vertically like a slot reel into the right one, marker sweeps, fish swims continuously.

shots.title: Tycoon
shots.show: Word card, same layout: the Chinese characters 大君 land at the top in amber with 'great + lord' under them. An arrow hop path runs down through 'taikun (Japanese)' to TYCOON landing huge in white. Then 'boss' appears struck through beside it and rolls into 'great lord', with the orange marker sweep. A small crown icon drops onto the last O.
shots.text: Tycoon: 'great lord', by way of Japanese
shots.motion: Characters stamp in, the arrow draws down hop by hop, each stop lights as reached, TYCOON slams in, the strike-and-roll, crown drops with a bounce.

shots.title: Typhoon
shots.show: Word card, same layout: two roots slide in from left and right: 大風 'big wind' (amber, Chinese) and 'Typhon, Greek storm monster' (cooler grey). They collide in the middle and fuse into TYPHOON, huge and white. Wind streaks whip across the frame behind the type and the letters wobble in the gusts. Orange marker sweeps under 'big wind'.
shots.text: Typhoon: Chinese 'big wind', plus a Greek monster
shots.motion: Roots slide in from opposite sides, merge with a flash, TYPHOON spins in a quarter turn and settles, wind particles stream left to right for the whole shot.

shots.title: Kowtow
shots.show: Word card, same layout: 叩頭 lands in amber, then splits into two halves labelled 'knock' and 'head'. KOWTOW lands huge in white; the whole word bows forward until its top touches a ground line, then straightens. Orange marker sweeps under 'knock head'.
shots.motion: Characters stamp, split apart with a tick, the English word tilts forward like a bow (twice, slow), dust puff where it touches the line, marker sweep.

shots.title: End card
shots.show: Four-word stack returns exactly as in shot 1 (same order, size and white type), now each word carries its small amber root beside it: fish sauce, great lord, big wind, knock head. A stamp 'FROM CHINESE' lands across the stack in fire orange.
shots.motion: Roots pop in one after another down the stack, the stamp slams with a short shake, a slow drift zoom keeps the frame moving to the end.
